category: PCB design rules: Manufacturing, High Speed, Placement & Signal Integrity types
description: Individual rule types from the Manufacturing, High Speed, Placement and Signal Integrity categories of Design > Rules / Constraint Manager, with their constraint fields, DRC behaviour and typical scopes.

tools.name: Minimum Annular Ring (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Minimum copper ring around a drilled hole, measured radially from hole edge to pad/via edge, on every layer where the pad or via has copper. Flags pads whose land is too small for the hole (including negative rings where the shape is smaller than the drill). Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Minimum Annular Ring
tools.example: Default rule 0.125 mm for All; a 0.1 mm rule scoped IsVia And (HoleSize <= 0.2mm) for HDI microvias if the fabricator allows it.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_MinimumAnnularRing; combine with Hole Size for a complete drill capability check.

tools.name: Acute Angle (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Minimum angle allowed between connected copper objects of the same net on the same layer, catching acid traps at track junctions. Check Tracks Only restricts the test to track objects and skips pad/track and arc junctions. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Acute Angle

parameters.name: Check Tracks Only
parameters.description: Ignore junctions involving pads, arcs, regions.

tools.example: Set Minimum Angle 90 and Check Tracks Only; violations at 45-degree stubs are removed with Route > Gloss Selected.
tools.notes: Works at net level by analysing contours, so overlapping copper of one net is treated as one shape.

tools.name: Hole Size (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Minimum and maximum drill diameter for pads and vias, either as Absolute values (default 1 mil to 100 mil) or as a Percent of the pad size (20-80%). A required default rule; scope by IsVia or IsPad to give different limits for vias and component holes. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Hole Size
tools.example: Rule IsVia: 0.2-0.6 mm; rule IsPad: 0.3-6.5 mm (mounting holes); default All 0.15-6.5 mm.
tools.notes: Slot holes are checked by their width; see also Hole To Hole Clearance and the PCB panel's Hole Size Editor mode.

tools.name: Layer Pairs (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Verifies that every via's start/stop layer pair matches one of the Via Types (drill pairs) defined in the Layer Stack Manager, so imported or scripted vias cannot use an unmanufacturable span. Enforced during interactive routing and by online/batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Layer Pairs
tools.example: Define Thru (Top-Bottom) and uVia (Top-L2) in Layer Stack Manager > Via Types; a via Top-L3 is then reported as a Layer Pairs violation.
tools.notes: Required default rule; query keyword IsRule_LayerPair.

tools.name: Hole To Hole Clearance (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Minimum edge-to-edge distance between drilled holes of pads and vias on any layer, preventing drill breakout and web failure. Allow Stacked Micro Vias exempts intentionally stacked uVias. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Hole To Hole Clearance
tools.example: Default 0.25 mm; enable Allow Stacked Micro Vias on HDI stacks using stacked uVia types.
tools.notes: Required default rule; query keyword IsRule_HoleToHoleClearance.

tools.name: Minimum Solder Mask Sliver (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Minimum width of solder-mask web between two adjacent mask openings (after Solder Mask Expansion), checked independently on top and bottom. Slivers narrower than the fabricator's capability peel off and cause bridging. Online (expensive) and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Minimum Solder Mask Sliver

parameters.name: Minimum Solder Mask Sliver
parameters.description: Minimum mask web width, e.g. 0.1 mm.

tools.example: Set 0.1 mm; resolve violations under fine-pitch QFPs by reducing the Solder Mask Expansion rule for that component class or gang-opening the mask.
tools.notes: Consider disabling Online checking for this rule on large boards.

tools.name: Silk To Solder Mask Clearance (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Clearance between silkscreen primitives and either solder-mask openings or exposed copper, so legend ink cannot land on pads. Replaces the legacy Silkscreen Over Component Pads rule. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Silk To Solder Mask Clearance

parameters.name: Clearance Checking Mode
parameters.description: Check Clearance To Exposed Copper | Check Clearance To Solder Mask Openings.

tools.example: Mode Check Clearance To Solder Mask Openings, 0.15 mm; fix violations by moving designators (Edit > Align commands or the designator Autoposition property) or shrinking text.
tools.notes: Required default rule; query keyword IsRule_SilkToSolderMaskClearance.

tools.name: Silk To Silk Clearance (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Minimum distance between silkscreen text and any other silkscreen object (outlines, other text), keeping designators legible and non-overlapping. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Silk To Silk Clearance

parameters.name: Silk Text to Any Silk Object Clearance

tools.example: Set 0.15 mm, then use the PCB Filter query IsDesignator And OnSilkscreen to select and batch-move violating designators.
tools.notes: Only text-to-object is tested (not outline-to-outline). Required default rule.

tools.name: Net Antennae (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Flags open-ended track/arc stubs on a net, including stubs terminated only by a via, that are longer than a tolerance. Such antennae are EMI radiators and often remnants of re-routing. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Net Antennae

parameters.name: Net Antennae Tolerance
parameters.description: Maximum permitted stub length (0 flags every stub).

tools.example: Tolerance 0 mm; clear violations with Route > Retrace or by deleting the stub via Edit > Select > Physical Connection.
tools.notes: Requires the Un-Routed Net rule enabled for connectivity analysis; required default rule.

tools.name: Board Outline Clearance (Manufacturing rule)
tools.description: Minimum clearance from fabricated objects (copper, silkscreen, components) to board edges, with a matrix distinguishing Outline Edge, Cavity Edge, Cutout Edge, Split Barrier and Split Continuation edges. Obeyed by interactive routing and the autorouter as well as online/batch DRC; a zero value lets objects cross the edge.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Manufacturing > Board Outline Clearance

parameters.name: Minimum Clearance
parameters.description: Single value for all object/edge combinations (default 10 mil).

tools.example: Set 0.3 mm copper-to-Outline Edge, 0.5 mm to Cutout Edge, and 0 for IsBoardOutline text; not created by default so add it explicitly.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_BoardOutlineClearance; the board shape must be defined for the check to run.

tools.name: Parallel Segment (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Limits how long two track segments of different nets may run parallel at a given separation, on the same layer or adjacent layers, to control crosstalk. Routed differential pairs are excluded and the scope cannot be layer-based. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Parallel Segment; binary scope

parameters.name: For a parallel gap of
parameters.description: Separation at or below which the limit applies.

tools.example: First InNetClass('CLK'), second All, Same Layer, gap 0.3 mm, limit 10 mm.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_ParallelSegment.

tools.name: Length (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Minimum and maximum routed length (or propagation delay) of a net or xSignal. Drives Interactive Length Tuning (target range) and is checked by online/batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Length; Constraint Manager: Electrical view > Length

parameters.name: Length Units / Delay Units
parameters.description: Constrain in mm/mil or in ps.

tools.example: Scope InxSignalClass('DDR_ADDR') Min 40 mm Max 42 mm; run Route > Interactive Length Tuning and watch the gauge (Shift+G).
tools.notes: For matching across nets use Matched Lengths instead.

tools.name: Matched Lengths (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Keeps the routed length/delay of nets or xSignals in the scope within a tolerance of each other (or of a Source Target xSignal). Options: Group Matched Lengths, Within Differential Pair Length with Dynamic Phase Matching (phase tolerance and matching distance) for intra-pair skew. Used by interactive and automatic length tuning and DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Matched Lengths

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: Maximum length/delay difference within the group.

parameters.name: Source Target
parameters.description: xSignal that others are matched to.

parameters.name: Within Differential Pair Length / Dynamic Phase Matching
parameters.description: Intra-pair skew control and its tolerance/matching distance.

tools.example: InxSignalClass('DDR_DQ0') tolerance 0.5 mm; separate rule InDifferentialPairClass('LVDS') Within Differential Pair Length tolerance 0.1 mm.
tools.notes: Multiple Matched Lengths rules can apply to one object; the tuning gauge shows the tightest constraint.

tools.name: Daisy Chain Stub Length (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Maximum branch (stub) length off the main trunk of a net routed with a daisy-chain topology, limiting reflections in multi-drop buses. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Daisy Chain Stub Length
tools.example: Routing Topology Daisy-Simple for InNetClass('SPI_BUS') plus Daisy Chain Stub Length 2 mm.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_DaisyChainStubLength.

tools.name: Vias Under SMD (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Allows or forbids vias under single-layer SMD pads (via-in-pad). Enforced by interactive routing, autorouting and online/batch DRC; the scope selects which SMD pads are governed.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Vias Under SMD
tools.example: Default disallow; rule InComponentClass('BGA_0.5mm') with Allow enabled for filled/capped via-in-pad escapes.
tools.notes: Pair with HasViaFeature('Filling') queries and the Via Types tab to make sure via-in-pad vias are plated over.

tools.name: Maximum Via Count (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Maximum number of vias permitted on each net in the scope, keeping critical signals on few layers. Target with InNet, InNetClass or InAnyNet. Online and batch DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Maximum Via Count
tools.example: InNetClass('CLOCKS') Maximum Via Count 2.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_MaximumViaCount; NetViaCount query keyword reports actual counts in the PCB Filter.

tools.name: Max Via Stub Length (Back Drilling) (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Identifies vias/pads whose unused barrel stub (from the last connected layer to the top or bottom) exceeds a length, marking them for back drilling with a specified oversize and tolerance. The drill depth comes from the Back Drills tab of the Layer Stack Manager; batch DRC only.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Max Via Stub Length (Back Drilling)

parameters.name: Max Stub Length
parameters.description: Stub length above which back drilling is required; Top Layer / Bottom Layer checkboxes.

parameters.name: Back Drill Oversize / Tolerance
parameters.description: Back-drill diameter increase over the via hole and its tolerance.

tools.example: InNetClass('SERDES') Max Stub Length 0.25 mm from Bottom, oversize 0.2 mm; define the back-drill layer span in Layer Stack Manager > Back Drills, then NC Drill output emits the back-drill files.
tools.notes: Query keywords BackDrillTop / BackDrillBottom select the resulting back-drill sites.

tools.name: Return Path (High Speed rule)
tools.description: Checks that a routed signal has a continuous reference (return) plane along its length on the layer(s) named by an impedance profile, reporting gaps, plane splits and excessive distance to stitching vias. Return path copper is formed from fills, regions and polygon pours on signal/plane layers. Batch DRC only.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > High Speed > Return Path

parameters.name: Impedance Profile
parameters.description: Profile whose reference layers define the return path.

parameters.name: Minimum Gap to Return Path
parameters.description: Smallest allowed distance from trace to the reference copper edge.

parameters.name: Max Stitch Via Distance
parameters.description: Optional maximum distance to a return via at layer changes.

tools.example: InNetClass('USB3') with profile 'DIFF90', Minimum Gap 0.2 mm, Max Stitch Via Distance 2 mm; run batch DRC and inspect violations in the PCB Rules And Violations panel.
tools.notes: Introduced in Altium Designer 19; query keyword IsRule_ReturnPath.

tools.name: Room Definition (Placement rule)
tools.description: Each room on the board is stored as a Room Definition rule: a rectangular or polygonal region on Top or Bottom in which the scoped components must stay Inside (or Outside). Fields include Room Locked, Components Locked, Layer and Confinement Mode; the outline itself is only editable graphically (Define button). Rooms also serve as scopes (WithinRoom) for other rules.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Placement > Room Definition; Design > Rooms > Place Rectangular/Polygonal Room

parameters.name: Room Locked / Components Locked
parameters.description: Prevent moving the room or the components in it.

parameters.name: Confinement Mode
parameters.description: Keep Objects Inside | Keep Objects Outside.

tools.example: Multi-channel designs create one room per channel automatically (scope InChannelClass('CHANNEL_1')); copy placement with Design > Rooms > Copy Room Formats.
tools.notes: A component may be in several rooms without conflict; online and batch DRC.

tools.name: Component Clearance (Placement rule)
tools.description: Minimum horizontal (and optionally vertical) distance between components, using their 3D bodies (mesh-accurate) or, with Check clearance by component boundary, their bounding outlines. Options: Vertical Clearance Mode Infinite/Specified, Show actual violation distances, Do not check components without 3D body. Online and batch DRC; also drives the collision feedback in 3D.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Placement > Component Clearance; binary scope

parameters.name: Vertical Clearance Mode / Minimum Vertical Clearance
parameters.description: Infinite (no overlap allowed) or a specified stacking gap.

tools.example: Default All-All 0.25 mm Infinite; rule InComponentClass('Connectors') to All 1 mm for rework access.
tools.notes: Requires 3D bodies or courtyards on footprints for meaningful results.

tools.name: Component Orientations (Placement rule)
tools.description: Declares the allowed rotations (0, 90, 180, 270, All Orientations) for components in the scope, intended for autoplacement and assembly conventions. Not currently enforced by DRC; kept for legacy autoplacer compatibility and documentation.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Placement > Component Orientations

parameters.name: Allowed Orientations
parameters.description: 0 Degrees | 90 Degrees | 180 Degrees | 270 Degrees | All Orientations.

tools.example: InComponentClass('Polarised') allow 0 and 180 degrees only, then check rotations manually via the PCB List panel (Rotation column).
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_ComponentRotations.

tools.name: Permitted Layers (Placement rule)
tools.description: Restricts components in the scope to the Top Layer and/or Bottom Layer, catching parts flipped to the wrong side (e.g. tall connectors that must be on top). Batch DRC only.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Placement > Permitted Layers
tools.example: InComponentClass('THT') Top Layer only; run batch DRC before assembly outputs.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_PermittedLayers.

tools.name: Nets to Ignore (Placement rule)
tools.description: Lists nets (typically power and ground) that the legacy autoplacer should disregard when clustering components by connectivity. Not observed by DRC.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Placement > Nets to Ignore
tools.example: Scope InNetClass('POWER') so decoupling caps are not pulled toward every IC by the placer.
tools.notes: Only meaningful with the legacy Cluster/Statistical placer.

tools.name: Height (Placement rule)
tools.description: Minimum, Preferred and Maximum component height for the scope; height is taken from the footprint's 3D bodies or, without bodies, the component Height property. Min/Max are tested by online/batch DRC, Preferred is used for 3D display. Scope by room (WithinRoom) to enforce enclosure keep-down zones.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Placement > Height
tools.example: Rule WithinRoom('UnderShield') Maximum 2 mm; default All Maximum 25 mm.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_MaxMinHeightConstraint.

tools.name: Signal Stimulus (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Defines the waveform injected at driver pins during Signal Integrity analysis: Constant Level, Single Pulse or Periodic Pulse with start level, start/stop times and period. Required for crosstalk runs (aggressors get the stimulus, victims a constant low).
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Signal Stimulus

parameters.name: Stimulus Kind
parameters.description: Constant Level | Single Pulse | Periodic Pulse.

parameters.name: Start Time / Stop Time / Period Time

tools.example: Periodic Pulse, Low start, 10 ns start, 60 ns stop, 20 ns period for a 50 MHz clock net class before Tools > Signal Integrity.
tools.notes: The analyser also needs IBIS/SI models on the drivers and Supply Nets rules.

tools.name: Overshoot - Rising Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum ringing above the settled high level on rising edges, in volts, evaluated by the Signal Integrity analyser's screening and reflection analysis; violating nets are listed in the SI panel with red markers.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Overshoot - Rising Edge
tools.example: 0.3 V for InNetClass('DDR'); check with Tools > Signal Integrity > Reflections.
tools.notes: Companion rules exist for falling-edge overshoot and rising/falling undershoot.

tools.name: Overshoot - Falling Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum ringing below the settled low (base) level on falling edges, in volts. Evaluated by Signal Integrity screening and reflection analysis.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Overshoot - Falling Edge
tools.example: 0.3 V for all nets; tighten to 0.15 V for InNetClass('ADC_IN').
tools.notes: Not created by default.

tools.name: Undershoot - Rising Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum dip below the top value (after the first overshoot) on rising edges, in volts; large undershoot risks false logic transitions.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Undershoot - Rising Edge
tools.example: 0.2 V for InNetClass('CLOCKS').
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_Undershoot_RisingEdge.

tools.name: Undershoot - Falling Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum rise above the base value on falling edges (ringing back toward the threshold), in volts.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Undershoot - Falling Edge
tools.example: 0.2 V; review results in the Signal Integrity panel and apply Termination Advisor suggestions.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_Undershoot_FallingEdge.

tools.name: Impedance (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Minimum and maximum characteristic impedance (ohms) a net's routing may present according to the SI analyser's transmission-line model derived from the layer stack. Distinct from the impedance profiles used for width calculation.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Impedance
tools.example: 45-55 ohm for InNetClass('SE50'); nets outside the range are flagged during Tools > Signal Integrity screening.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_MaxMinImpedance.

tools.name: Signal Top Value (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Minimum voltage a signal must settle to in its high state (VOH check) as computed by the SI analyser.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Signal Top Value
tools.example: 2.4 V for 3.3 V LVCMOS nets.
tools.notes: Pair with Signal Base Value for the low state.

tools.name: Signal Base Value (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum voltage a signal may settle to in its low state (VOL check) in Signal Integrity analysis.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Signal Base Value
tools.example: 0.4 V for 3.3 V logic nets.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_SignalBaseValue.

tools.name: Flight Time - Rising Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum interconnect-induced delay on rising edges: the time between the driver reaching threshold into a reference load and the receiver reaching threshold through the actual routing, in seconds.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Flight Time - Rising Edge
tools.example: 1.5 ns for InNetClass('DDR_DQ').
tools.notes: Computed by reflection analysis; needs IBIS models with timing data.

tools.name: Flight Time - Falling Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum interconnect-induced delay on falling edges, in seconds.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Flight Time - Falling Edge
tools.example: 1.5 ns for InNetClass('DDR_DQ').
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_FlightTime_FallingEdge.

tools.name: Slope - Rising Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum rise time (threshold-to-high) allowed at the receiver, in seconds; slow edges caused by heavy loading or long stubs are flagged.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Slope - Rising Edge
tools.example: 2 ns on InNetClass('CLOCKS').
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_MaxSlope_RisingEdge.

tools.name: Slope - Falling Edge (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Maximum fall time allowed at the receiver, in seconds.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Slope - Falling Edge
tools.example: 2 ns on InNetClass('CLOCKS').
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_MaxSlope_FallingEdge.

tools.name: Supply Nets (Signal Integrity rule)
tools.description: Declares a net (or net class) as a power supply with a given voltage so the SI analyser treats it as a reference rather than a signal and does not compute length/delay for it. Created automatically for nets with power ports when transferring from schematic; add rules for supplies named differently.
tools.usage: Design > Rules > Signal Integrity > Supply Nets

parameters.name: Voltage
parameters.description: Supply voltage for the scoped nets.

tools.example: InNet('VCC3V3') Voltage 3.3; InNet('GND') Voltage 0.
tools.notes: Query keyword IsRule_SupplyNets; missing supply rules produce warnings in the Signal Integrity setup dialog.
